hypothesis.description: When the Legacy Payment API times out after committing a refund, the payment worker retries without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate refund to be processed.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This experiment tests whether the system violates the network-level idempotency invariant by triggering the payment service's documented 'duplicate charge on retry (always, no dedup)' failure mode. The timeout intervention creates the ambiguous state that leads to retry, while the payment service contract guarantees duplicates on retry without idempotency keys.

interventions.description: The request times out, leaving the agent unsure whether the side effect committed.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

interventions.description: Payment commits but its response is lost, leaving the agent unsure whether the charge succeeded.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

hypothesis.experimentRationale: The same fixed sequence is applied to every case; the baseline does not adapt to evidence.

interventions.description: A batch partially fails; some items succeed while others fail, challenging compensation logic.
The agent loses in-memory state without a checkpoint, so recovery may replay operations.
A worker crashes and loses in-memory state; the agent must restart and recover.

hypothesis.experimentRationale: The same fixed sequence is applied to every case; the baseline does not adapt to evidence.

interventions.description: The external API returns 429 responses, potentially triggering repeated retries.
The agent sends the same request twice; without idempotency, both requests can cause a charge.

response.text:
{
  "description": "When a fulfillment worker restarts after Stripe commits a charge but before the acknowledgement is recorded, the agent loses in-memory state, attempts recovery using the last persisted checkpoint, and retries the payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge despite the checkpoint tracking the original intent.",
  "rationale": "The previous experiment showed that kill_worker + missing_idempotency_key triggers duplicate charges, proving rule r04-network-idempotency is violated. This new hypothesis distinguishes between pure in-memory loss versus checkpoint-based recovery behavior by testing whether durable state (Storage checkpoint) fails to prevent the duplicate when the worker restarts after commit but before acknowledgement recording.",
  "expectedInvariant": "r03-durable-execution",
  "interventions": ["kill_worker", "lose_state", "missing_idempotency_key"],
  "confidence": 0.75
}

hypothesis.description: When a fulfillment worker restarts after Stripe commits a charge but before the acknowledgement is recorded, the agent loses in-memory state and retries the payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This experiment isolates the interaction between worker restart timing (after remote commit, before ack) and idempotency key usage. If a duplicate charge occurs, it confirms the failure mode 'Duplicate charge without idempotency key' in Stripe Payment API and 'Retries without idempotency key' in AI Agent. If no duplicate occurs, the system correctly handles the restart via checkpoint recovery or idempotency.

interventions.description: A worker crashes and loses in-memory state; the agent must restart and recover.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

interventionSequence.hypothesis: When a fulfillment worker restarts after Stripe commits a charge but before the acknowledgement is recorded, the agent loses in-memory state and retries the payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge.

interventions.description: Payment commits but its response is lost, leaving the agent unsure whether the charge succeeded.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

hypothesis.experimentRationale: The same fixed sequence is applied to every case; the baseline does not adapt to evidence.

interventions.description: A batch partially fails; some items succeed while others fail, challenging compensation logic.
The agent loses in-memory state without a checkpoint, so recovery may replay operations.
A worker crashes and loses in-memory state; the agent must restart and recover.

hypothesis.experimentRationale: The same fixed sequence is applied to every case; the baseline does not adapt to evidence.

interventions.description: The external API returns 429 responses, potentially triggering repeated retries.

Large state writes saturate storage IOPS and increase primary storage usage.

response.text:
{
  "description": "When a worker crashes mid-workflow after a payment commits but before the checkpoint is persisted (kill_worker + lose_state), the agent recovers without the payment confirmation and retries without an idempotency key (missing_idempotency_key), causing a duplicate charge while the reported cost metric only reflects the retried attempt.",
  "rationale": "The prior experiment proved that drop_response + missing_idempotency_key causes underreported cost (r10). This experiment isolates whether crash-induced state loss (kill_worker + lose_state) combined with missing idempotency produces the same invariant violation via a different failure path, distinguishing crash recovery semantics from network loss semantics.",
  "expectedInvariant": "r10-unit-economics",
  "interventions": ["kill_worker", "lose_state", "missing_idempotency_key"],
  "confidence": 0.85
}

hypothesis.description: When a payment response is lost (drop_response) and the agent retries without an idempotency key (missing_idempotency_key), the reported cost metric captures only the initial successful attempt while the retry causes an undetected duplicate charge, violating unit economics by underreporting total work performed.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This experiment isolates whether the cost metric tracks retries by combining response loss (which triggers retries) with missing idempotency keys (which allows duplicates). It distinguishes between cost underreporting due to retry logic gaps vs. idempotency enforcement failures.

interventions.description: Payment commits but its response is lost, leaving the agent unsure whether the charge succeeded.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

interventionSequence.hypothesis: When a payment response is lost (drop_response) and the agent retries without an idempotency key (missing_idempotency_key), the reported cost metric captures only the initial successful attempt while the retry causes an undetected duplicate charge, violating unit economics by underreporting total work performed.

hypothesis.description: When a worker crashes mid-workflow after a payment commits but before the checkpoint is persisted (kill_worker + lose_state), the agent recovers without the payment confirmation and retries without an idempotency key (missing_idempotency_key), causing a duplicate charge while the reported cost metric only reflects the retried attempt.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: The prior experiment proved that drop_response + missing_idempotency_key causes underreported cost (r10). This experiment isolates whether crash-induced state loss (kill_worker + lose_state) combined with missing idempotency produces the same invariant violation via a different failure path, distinguishing crash recovery semantics from network loss semantics.

interventions.description: A worker crashes and loses in-memory state; the agent must restart and recover.
The agent loses in-memory state without a checkpoint, so recovery may replay operations.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

interventionSequence.hypothesis: When a worker crashes mid-workflow after a payment commits but before the checkpoint is persisted (kill_worker + lose_state), the agent recovers without the payment confirmation and retries without an idempotency key (missing_idempotency_key), causing a duplicate charge while the reported cost metric only reflects the retried attempt.

interventions.description: A batch partially fails; some items succeed while others fail, challenging compensation logic.
The agent loses in-memory state without a checkpoint, so recovery may replay operations.
A worker crashes and loses in-memory state; the agent must restart and recover.

interventions.description: The external API returns 429 responses, potentially triggering repeated retries.

{
  "description": "When the Legacy Payment API delays a refund response beyond the timeout, the AI Agent loses in-memory state (e.g., due to a worker crash) and recovers without a checkpoint, causing it to retry the refund without an idempotency key. The first request may have already committed, resulting in a duplicate refund.",
  "rationale": "The prior experiment confirmed that timeout + missing idempotency key causes duplicates (r04-network-idempotency). This hypothesis distinguishes whether the missing idempotency key on retry is caused by the agent losing state and failing to persist the idempotency key before the crash (r03-durable-execution), rather than the agent simply forgetting to generate one. It tests the interaction of timeout, state loss, and missing idempotency key.",
  "expectedInvariant": "r03-durable-execution",
  "interventions": [
    "timeout",
    "kill_worker",
    "missing_idempotency_key"
  ],
  "confidence": 0.85
}

hypothesis.description: When the Legacy Payment API times out on a refund request, the AI Agent retries without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate refund because the first request may have committed before the timeout.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: The Legacy Payment API contract guarantees 'Timeout with ambiguous state' and 'Duplicate charge on retry (always, no dedup)', and the AI Agent has a failure mode of 'Retries without idempotency key'. The invariant r04-network-idempotency requires idempotency keys for safe retries. This experiment tests whether the system violates that invariant by applying the missing_idempotency_key and timeout interventions to trigger a duplicate refund.

interventions.description: The request times out, leaving the agent unsure whether the side effect committed.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

interventionSequence.hypothesis: When the Legacy Payment API times out on a refund request, the AI Agent retries without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate refund because the first request may have committed before the timeout.

{
  "description": "When a fulfillment worker restarts after Stripe commits a charge but before the acknowledgement is persisted, the worker loses in-memory state and restarts without a stored idempotency key, causing it to retry the payment without deduplication and produce a duplicate charge.",
  "rationale": "The previous experiment proved r04-network-idempotency (idempotency prevents duplicates) but also surfaced r03-durable-execution as an unknown rule. This experiment isolates the durable-execution gap: even with idempotency available, if the worker crashes before checkpointing the key, recovery cannot reuse it. Using kill_worker + missing_idempotency_key together tests whether the system violates r03-durable-execution by allowing a duplicate charge when the key is lost in the restart window.",
  "expectedInvariant": "r03-durable-execution",
  "interventions": ["kill_worker", "missing_idempotency_key"],
  "confidence": 0.85
}

hypothesis.description: When a fulfillment worker restarts after Stripe commits a charge but before the acknowledgement is persisted, the worker loses in-memory state and may retry the payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This directly tests the scenario in the system description: a remote operation (Stripe charge) commits, then the worker restarts (kill_worker) before recording the ack. On recovery, the agent lacks the idempotency key (missing_idempotency_key) and cannot deduplicate, violating r04-network-idempotency.

A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

{
  "description": "Under database pool exhaustion during payment processing, the agent's transaction times out while Stripe commits the charge, causing a retry without an idempotency key and a duplicate charge, while the reported cost metric only reflects the final successful attempt.",
  "rationale": "This distinguishes r04-network-idempotency (already confirmed) from r05-distributed-sagas by introducing a database-layer failure (pool exhaustion) that triggers the same retry behavior but through a different path—saga compensation logic failure rather than direct network issues. It also tests r10-unit-economics (cost metric accuracy) under database-induced retries.",
  "expectedInvariant": "r05-distributed-sagas",
  "interventions": ["drop_response", "missing_idempotency_key", "rate_limit"],
  "confidence": 0.75
}

hypothesis.description: Under network timeout or response loss, the agent retries a Stripe payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge, but the reported cost metric only reflects the final successful attempt.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This experiment isolates whether the cost metric accounts for all retry attempts (including duplicate side effects) or only the last recorded success. Competing explanations include: the metric correctly aggregates all attempts, or the agent never retries without a key. The intervention directly triggers the failure mode 'Duplicate charge without idempotency key' from Stripe and 'Retries without idempotency key' from the agent.

interventions.description: The request times out, leaving the agent unsure whether the side effect committed.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

hypothesis.description: Under worker crash and state loss, the agent restarts and retries a Stripe payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge, but the reported cost metric only reflects the final successful attempt.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: The prior experiment showed duplicate charges and cost metric undercounting under network timeout with missing idempotency key. This experiment distinguishes whether the same duplicate-charge-and-underreporting behavior occurs when the retry is triggered by worker crash/state loss rather than network timeout, isolating the agent's recovery logic as the root cause.

interventions.description: A worker crashes and loses in-memory state; the agent must restart and recover.
The agent loses in-memory state without a checkpoint, so recovery may replay operations.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

interventionSequence.hypothesis: Under worker crash and state loss, the agent restarts and retries a Stripe payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge, but the reported cost metric only reflects the final successful attempt.

hypothesis.description: Under database pool exhaustion during payment processing, the agent's transaction times out while Stripe commits the charge, causing a retry without an idempotency key and a duplicate charge, while the reported cost metric only reflects the final successful attempt.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This distinguishes r04-network-idempotency (already confirmed) from r05-distributed-sagas by introducing a database-layer failure (pool exhaustion) that triggers the same retry behavior but through a different path—saga compensation logic failure rather than direct network issues. It also tests r10-unit-economics (cost metric accuracy) under database-induced retries.

interventions.description: Payment commits but its response is lost, leaving the agent unsure whether the charge succeeded.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.
The external API returns 429 responses, potentially triggering repeated retries.

interventionSequence.hypothesis: Under database pool exhaustion during payment processing, the agent's transaction times out while Stripe commits the charge, causing a retry without an idempotency key and a duplicate charge, while the reported cost metric only reflects the final successful attempt.

{
  "description": "Agent loses in-memory state during payment processing, restarts from durable checkpoint, and retries Stripe payment without idempotency key causing duplicate charge",
  "rationale": "Experiments 1 and 2 tested kill_worker + missing_idempotency_key with and without drop_response. Both showed zero duplicateDollars, suggesting either r03-durable-execution prevents duplicate retries after restart, or the agent doesn't retry payments after checkpoint recovery. Testing lose_state (loss of in-memory state without checkpoint) with missing_idempotency_key distinguishes whether the agent only retries when it has no durable recovery path, which would violate r04-network-idempotency.",
  "expectedInvariant": "r04-network-idempotency",
  "interventions": ["lose_state", "missing_idempotency_key"],
  "confidence": 0.7
}

hypothesis.description: Agent loses in-memory state during payment processing, restarts from durable checkpoint, and retries Stripe payment without idempotency key causing duplicate charge
hypothesis.experimentRationale: Tests whether the combination of durable checkpointing (Storage guarantee) and bounded recovery (Process Supervisor guarantee) prevents duplicate charges when agent loses in-memory state (AI Agent failure mode) and retries without idempotency key (Stripe failure mode). This distinguishes between checkpointing correctness vs. idempotency enforcement.

interventions.description: A worker crashes and loses in-memory state; the agent must restart and recover.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

findings.message: Model calls s-e59 and s-e60 have the same input hash, but the trace does not establish a verified resume boundary.
findings.repro: Trace run s-run-experiment-812-812: compare model-call input hashes for spans s-e59 and s-e60, then inspect explicit checkpoint/resume fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist a checkpoint and require an explicit resume_of reference before treating a later model call as re-execution.

hypothesis.description: Payment commits successfully but response is lost due to network drop; agent restarts from durable checkpoint, has no in-memory state of the payment, and retries without idempotency key causing duplicate charge
hypothesis.experimentRationale: Previous experiment tested kill_worker + missing_idempotency_key but showed no duplicates (duplicateDollars=0), suggesting the agent may not retry on clean restart. This experiment adds drop_response to create ambiguity about payment success, forcing a retry decision that distinguishes between 'agent correctly recovers state from checkpoint' vs 'agent loses payment context and blindly retries'
